style.name: K1-minimal 1 · plain
style.block: A 2D key frame from a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, shown in the reference image. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every shape has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. A soft paper grain on every piece, and soft violet cast shadows on the wall and floor from a warm light at the upper left. Hands are plain round paper circles floating beside the body: no arms, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.
style.world: Righteousness by Faith, a narrated explainer film about how God makes people righteous. It has two registers: an IDEA beat is a light parchment page with figures and props cut from paper laid on it; a STORY beat is a cardboard diorama of three to five layered paper planes under a simple two- or three-stop gradient sky. The everyman is a small figure cut from plain cool grey paper: a round bald head, a simple plain tunic, circle hands. Crowds are grey paper figures of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus wears a plain white robe with a gold sash. The colour script: scarlet only for sin (stains), white for the robe, gold only for God's word and the verdict; everything else calm creams, taupes, teals and peaches.

THE SCENE (the same in every style): one key frame from the cold open of a narrated animated explainer film. A courtroom built as a paper diorama on a light parchment page, in three layered paper planes standing one behind another with a little depth between them. Colours: a light, calm parchment world of cream and warm taupe papers; the judge's robe a deep brown-black; scarlet only on the stains; gold only on the verdict.

Back plane: the far wall, tall sheets of pale toned parchment paper with torn edges; two tall plain pillars of a slightly deeper tone, one near the left edge of the frame and one near the right edge; the torn edge of the floor running along the bottom. The walls are bare: no windows, no pictures, no emblems, seals, flags, scales or symbols, and no writing.

Middle plane: the judge's bench, a tall, wide, wooden-looking desk of warm taupe paper that fills the right half of the frame, from just right of the centre to near the right edge. Its front has three tall recessed panels side by side, and a darker rim runs along its top. A small dark wooden gavel and its small round sounding block sit on the bench top near its right end. Behind the bench, centred over it, sits the judge, seen from the chest up: a big round bald head of plain grey paper, almost twice the size of the accused's head, with a calm, unreadable face; a dark, nearly black robe; two small white bands hanging side by side at the collar, like a barrister's bands. He wears no wig and no glasses. His hands are plain grey circles.

Front plane, nearest to us: the accused, standing on the floor at the left third of the frame, small, only about half as tall as the bench: a plain everyman cut from grey paper, with a round bald grey head, grey circle hands, and a simple plain tunic of the same grey paper with two scarlet stains on its chest, one large splotch and one small one. Right beside the accused, between them and the bench, a neat stack of about nine loose blank paper sheets, slightly askew, piled up to the accused's shoulder: the evidence.

Only these two figures are in the court: the judge and the accused. Nobody else.

THE MOMENT: the judge says "righteous". He leans forward a little, and his circle hand brings the gavel down hard onto its sounding block, with a few short impact strokes. At the same instant the verdict is stamped across the front of the bench: a torn cream paper label laid across the three front panels, tilted slightly upward to the right, bearing one word in large, bold, gold serif capital letters: RIGHTEOUS. The label has just slammed on, with a small burst of gold at its edges. The accused lifts their head and looks up at the judge, startled, brows raised.

THE CAMERA: straight on and at eye level, like a stage seen from the stalls; a medium-wide shot: the floor along the bottom fifth of the frame, the top rim of the bench a little above the middle, the judge's head in the upper right, the accused and the evidence in the lower left.

TEXT: the only word anywhere in the image is RIGHTEOUS, on the label, spelled exactly R-I-G-H-T-E-O-U-S. No other letters, numbers, captions, signatures or labels anywhere; the evidence sheets are blank.

RULES: Shade with colour: every shaded side and every cast shadow turns its hue toward the complement of the light (violet-blue under a warm light), never black and never plain grey; outlines may be dark. Even the grey paper's shaded side leans violet. Hands are plain round circles: no thumbs, no fingers. No crosses, church buildings, religious symbols, logos or emblems anywhere. A clean, calm, finished animated-film frame, not a photograph and not a character sheet.

Pull back to the three icons with the open hand under them, all lit.
